scope.purpose: Show the people (or teams) involved in an object as a compact row of overlapping avatars, with a count of the others.
useCases: The assignees of a task or the reviewers of a document in a table cell or a card.
The participants of a meeting or the members of a project, capped by max with a +N count.
A count of everyone when the application shows only the first few (total).
exclusions: A list of everyone or a profile on activation: composed by the integration (Popover or Tooltip on a wrapping button).
Interactive avatars or +N inside the group in this version.
alternatives: A single Avatar with the name beside it.
A list of people with names (a table, a list) when every person matters.
A Counter with a label when only the number matters.

fixtures: Portrait pictures of the Avatar examples.

decisionsTaken: Built in wave 5 together with Avatar (user at the wave 5 contract gate, round 1 (2026-11-13): "AvatarGroup, je pense que c'est une bonne idée de le faire maintenant en même temps que Avatar, au moins ce sera fait").
A component of its own (like ButtonGroup), family content, depending on Avatar; it passes size and shape to its avatars.
Overlap of a quarter of the avatar size (component.avatar-group.overlap.{size} = 6, 8, 10, 12, 16 px); the first avatar is on top (reading order).

Ring of border.width.strong (2 px) in color.surface.default around each avatar; on another surface the integration sets the ring color (custom property). A cut-out mask was considered: it works on any backdrop but is harder to reproduce in Figma and for square shapes.
max 5 by default and counted with the +N box (the group never shows more than max boxes, as in common libraries); total for a number known by the application beyond the avatars given.
The +N box is an Avatar whose new initials prop holds the text, so that it shares the Avatar typography and colors without binding Avatar tokens; capped at +99.
Exposed as a list named by label; the +N box is named "3 more" (count followed by moreLabel).

Implementation: Svelte API: the people are an `avatars` array (name, src, initials) rather than Avatar children, so that max, total and the +N box are known during server rendering; the contract part avatars accepts Avatar, which the group renders.
Round 2: stacking B, each avatar above the previous one (document order, no z-index).
Final consistency pass (user, 2026-11-22): option A, a max of 1 counts as 2 (one avatar and the +N box).
nextAction: Pull request wave/5 to main; Done once merged.
implementationNotes: Exports AvatarGroup and the types AvatarGroupProps, AvatarGroupItem.
Each avatar is drawn above the previous one by document order (no z-index; round 2 of the implementation review); the +N box, last, is drawn above the others.
The ring is a box-shadow outside each avatar; the group has no padding for it, so that it aligns with neighbouring content. In forced colors the ring becomes a Canvas outline on the item.
The ring color is the custom property --ggb-avatar-group-ringColor, which an integration sets on the group for another surface.
